checkpoints.note: The current request has already passed Thread TLV lookup and the vacuous `networkData.IsValid()` check, so leader-side registration now begins on the attacker-controlled Network Data bytes.

This is the first project-code statement on the crashing path after lower-layer message/container parsing has admitted the current Server Data request. The immediately following `networkData.IsValid()` check does not constrain inner Network Data bytes because `ThreadNetworkDataTlv::IsValid()` always returns true.

The fixing diff adds the missing guard `(borderRouter->GetLength() != borderRouterBase->GetLength())` ahead of `memcmp` on this path. With that extra check, the witness would return `rval = true` without reading past the current stack `networkData` buffer.
